title_en: De Sua Ebrietate (On His Own Drunkenness)
description: A pamphlet written by Antony defending his drinking habits against Cicero's attacks in the Philippics. Known only from Cicero's rebuttal (Phil. 2). No text survives.
Silver denarii issued by Antony to pay his legions before Actium. Features a war galley on the obverse and legionary eagle between two standards on the reverse with legion numbers (LEG I–XXIII).
location: Museums and private collections worldwide. Examples: British Museum, ANS, BM.

description: Silver tetradrachms and denarii featuring portraits of Antony and Cleopatra. Issued in eastern mints, possibly Antioch or Alexandria.
location: British Museum, American Numismatic Society, other major collections.

description: Letters written by Antony to Cicero, Octavian, and others. Fragments are preserved in Cicero's correspondence (Ad Atticum, Ad Familiares) and quoted in Suetonius (Aug. 4, 69). Several letters between Antony and Octavian are preserved in Suetonius and Appian, though authenticity is not always certain.
